facts.value: on or before the next regular payday
facts.summary: North Carolina: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due on or before the next regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: Employees whose employment is discontinued for any reason shall be paid all wages due on or before the next regular payday either through the regular pay channels or by trackable mail if requested by the employee in writing.
facts.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 95-25.7, Payment to separated employees

facts.value: on or before the next regular payday
facts.summary: North Carolina: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due on or before the next regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: Employees whose employment is discontinued for any reason shall be paid all wages due on or before the next regular payday either through the regular pay channels or by trackable mail if requested by the employee in writing.
facts.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 95-25.7, Payment to separated employees

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: North Carolina basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $7.25.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $7.25 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 Premium pay is required after 45 hours a week in seasonal amusements or recreational establishments.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: North Carolina independent contractor reporting required? (per OCSE): No

facts.summary: North Carolina new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Within 20 days of start date
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Within 20 days of start date

facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services

facts.summary: North Carolina is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
